extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO examiners/staff who prepare or decide petitions to the Director
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from the MPEP on when and how to file petitions to the Director of the USPTO, what they must contain, timeliness and fee rules, routing/decision authority, and which office/official decides particular petition types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate paper for each distinct subject (37 CFR 1.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Since different matters may be considered by different branches or sections of the Office, each distinct subject, inquiry or order must be contained in a separate paper to avoid confusion and delay in answering papers dealing with different subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects provided for on a single Office or WIPO form may be contained in a single paper.  (Cites 37 CFR 1.4(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for petition to the Director (37 CFR 1.181(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may be taken to the Director: (1) from any action or requirement of any examiner in ex parte prosecution of an application, or in ex parte or inter partes prosecution of a reexamination proceeding which is not subject to appeal to the PTAB or to the court; (2) in cases in which a statute or the rules specify that the matter is to be determined directly by or reviewed by the Director; and (3) to invoke the supervisory authority of the Director in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For petitions involving PTAB action see § 41.3. This defines the universe of matters that can be brought to the Director under §1.181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a petition (37 CFR 1.181(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition must contain a statement of the facts involved, the point or points to be reviewed, and the action requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefs or memoranda in support should accompany or be embodied in the petition; where facts are to be proven, proof in the form of affidavits or declarations (and exhibits, if any) must accompany the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior reconsideration and repeated action may be required (37 CFR 1.181(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition is taken from an examiner's action in prosecution, it may be required that there have been a proper request for reconsideration (§1.111) and a repeated action by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may be directed by the Director to furnish a written statement, within a specified time, setting forth the reasons for his or her decision on matters averred in the petition and supplying a copy to the petitioner. Examiner responses may be formal statements or informal memoranda (see MPEP § 711.03(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for petitions (37 CFR 1.181(d) and related provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a fee is required for a petition to the Director, the appropriate section will indicate it; if any required fee does not accompany the petition, the petition will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 10.20 may be used where an insufficient fee was filed. Petition fees are set forth in 37 CFR 1.17 (and 1.17(f) for certain petitions under §1.182/1.183).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing is exceptional (37 CFR 1.181(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral hearing will not be granted except when considered necessary by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect petitions to be resolved on papers unless the Director (or delegate) determines an oral hearing is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a petition does not stay other periods or proceedings (37 CFR 1.181(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere filing of a petition will not stay any period for reply that may be running against the application, nor act as a stay of other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a petition to vacate a final rejection filed within two months does not extend the period for reply even if the petition is not decided within that period. If the petition is later granted and the applicant timely filed a full reply, the case is not abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness rule — two-month filing period (37 CFR 1.181(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition under this part not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice from which relief is requested may be dismissed as untimely, except as otherwise provided; this two-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month benchmark applies to petitions under part 1 unless a different period is specified by the particular rule (e.g., §§1.377, 1.378, 1.740). The two-month period is not extendible under §1.136(a) because it is within the Director's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for accepting an untimely petition (decision-maker discretion guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deciding officials may reasonably exercise discretion to accept a petition filed more than two months after the mailing date where accepting it would avoid unnecessary delays in prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exhaustive factors to consider when accepting an untimely petition: (1) petitioner engaged in significant constructive efforts with the examiner to resolve the issue outside petitions; (2) the examiner agreed, on the written record, to perform an action that would resolve the issue, but failed to do so; (3) extenuating circumstances such as health, pandemic, natural disaster, etc. If accepted late, the decision should articulate the reason and explain how the two-month period was calculated; if dismissed as untimely, inform petitioner arguments on timeliness may be presented in a renewed petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirement for petitions under §§1.182 and 1.183
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition seeking a decision under §1.182 or any petition under §1.183 must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in §1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All petitions under these sections without the fee should be dismissed. This applies to petitions seeking discretionary decisions under §§1.182 (questions not specifically provided for) and 1.183 (suspension of rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard petition checklist (MPEP guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition should include: (1) a statement of the type of relief requested and the authorizing provision of statute or rules, if applicable; (2) a statement of the relevant facts; (3) an identification of the points that are to be reviewed; and (4) the fee, where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.4(c) requires a separate petition for each distinct subject; ordinarily file under a single authorizing provision (e.g., 37 CFR 1.181). Concurrent petitions may be filed but petitioners have often benefited by delaying certain petitions until an earlier petition is decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for handling petitions and examiner statements (MPEP §1002.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions and the respective application files are sent to the official having delegated authority to decide the petition; the petition may be referred to the examiner for a formal statement under 37 CFR 1.181(c) or for an informal memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a formal statement is made, a copy is mailed to the petitioner by the examiner unless directed otherwise; if an informal memorandum is requested, no copy is mailed to the petitioner by the examiner. Use Form paragraph 10.30 to generate header information for petition decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation principle and finality of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may delegate authority to decide petitions to appropriate PTO officials; where authority has been delegated, a denial of a petition is a final agency decision, while a dismissal or denial without prejudice is not a final agency decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions by Technology Center Directors should avoid language suggesting a dismissed petition is a final agency decision; sample dismissal language is provided to clarify non-final status and the two-month reconsideration period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions decided by the Deputy Commissioner who oversees the Office of Petitions (MPEP §1002.02(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A long list of specific petition types are assigned to the Deputy Commissioner (Office of Petitions/Patent Legal Administration/MPEP staff) for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated items include (but are not limited to): petitions to revive abandoned applications based on unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137); petitions under §1.183 for waiver/suspension of rules; petitions invoking supervisory authority under §1.181; petitions for unintentionally delayed foreign or domestic priority/benefit claims (§1.55(e), §1.78); petitions to defer issuance (1.314); express abandonment after issue fee (1.313(c)(3)); petitions relating to patent term adjustment and restoration; petitions relating to filing date and conversions between provisional/nonprovisional; petitions to change entity status (1.28/1.29); petitions to issue corrected patents (1.322(b)); petitions to expunge/expunge assignment info (1.59/1.182) and many others (items 1–50 listed in the MPEP). See MPEP §1002.02(b) for the full enumerated list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions and requests decided by Technology Center Directors (MPEP §1002.02(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology Center (TC) Directors have delegated authority to decide numerous petitions arising in applications assigned to their TCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of petitions decided by TC Directors include reopening prosecution or reinstating a rejection after a PTAB decision, petitions under §1.144 after restriction requirement, supervisory petitions under §1.181 for ex parte examiner actions not subject to appeal (e.g., prematureness of final rejection, refusal to enter amendments, resetting reply periods for delayed mail delivery, requirements for information under §1.105), petitions under §1.113 (objections/requirements by examiners), extension requests under §1.136(b) in TC cases, certain restriction/traversal petitions, petitions to expunge papers submitted under MPEP §724.02 or as part of an IDS, and many other TC-specific matters (see MPEP §1002.02(c) for full list and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions decided by the Director of the Technology Center who Oversees Licensing and Review (MPEP §1002.02(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional authority is delegated to the Director of the Technology Center who Oversees Licensing and Review for security/defense and secrecy-related petitions and certain foreign filing/licensing matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated authorities include petitions under 35 U.S.C. 267 for armament/defense-related U.S.-owned applications, petitions under §1.103(f) to suspend action when publication might be detrimental to public safety/defense, petitions under 37 CFR 5.12(b) for foreign license to file, petitions for rescission/modification of secrecy orders (37 CFR 5.4/5.5), petitions relating to DOE/NASA property rights statements, foreign filing licenses under 35 U.S.C. 184, and review of security/government interest matters, among others (see MPEP §1002.02(c)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions decided in the Central Reexamination Unit (MPEP §1002.02(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to decide petitions arising in reexamination proceedings is delegated to the CRU Director (and where noted, to CRU SPRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers petitions under 37 CFR 1.181(a)(1) from examiner actions in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings, requests for reconsideration of decisions on such petitions, and other reexamination-specific petitions; see MPEP §1002.02(c)(4) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions and matters decided by other delegated offices (grouped delegations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP identifies numerous other delegated decision authorities: Director of Tech Center 2900 (design applications), Director of OPAP, Director of Office of Data Management, Deputy Director of USPTO (PTAB-related petitions), Director of International Patent Legal Administration (PCT/national stage/Hague matters), Deputy Commissioner for Patents who oversees IT for e-Office issues, Director of Certificates of Correction Branch, Director of Office of Enrollment and Discipline, Solicitor/General Counsel offices, Central Reexamination Unit, and Technology Centers generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each delegation section enumerates specific petition types and limits on further delegation. See MPEP §1002.02 subsections (d)–(t) for the assigned lists, routing, and special handling (e.g., PTAB-related petitions forwarded to the Office of the Solicitor when decided by the Deputy Director).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and sample decision language
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP provides form paragraphs for common petition decision actions (e.g., ¶10.20 for dismissal due to insufficient fee; ¶10.30 for petition header information) and suggests language for TC Director dismissals to clarify non-finality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested dismissal language: 'The petition filed [date X] is dismissed. This is not a final agency decision. See MPEP §1002.02. Any request for reconsideration or higher level review of this decision not filed within two months of the mailing date of this decision may be dismissed as untimely. This two-month period is not extendable. See 37 CFR 1.181(f).' Use MPEP form paragraphs to ensure consistent decision formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on sequencing and strategic filing of concurrent petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Although concurrent petitions seeking relief from the same action may be filed, many prior petitioners have benefitted by delaying the filing of petitions under §1.182 or §1.183 until after they receive a decision on a petition seeking supervisory review under §1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the mere filing of a petition does not stay reply periods and because different petitions may be decided by different officials with different finality consequences, consider sequencing petitions strategically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explain timeliness calculation when dismissing as untimely
rubrics_metrics.description: If the deciding official determines that a petition will be dismissed as untimely, the decision should include an explanation of how the two-month period was calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision should inform petitioner that arguments on the issue of timeliness may be presented in a renewed petition. When accepting an untimely petition, the reason should be articulated in the decision to ensure clarity of the record.
